output.threat_model.summary: SQLite3::Database's C extension is the sole owner of the sqlite3* connection handle. Untrusted data reaches it as (a) Ruby-level arguments from the host application -- database filename, VFS name, options hash, SQL fragments, UDF/aggregate names, busy timeout, callables -- and (b) values flowing back out of the SQLite engine into Ruby callbacks: SQL text handed to the trace hook, sqlite3_value arguments handed to registered scalar/aggregate functions, authorizer argument strings, error messages, and the PRAGMA encoding row. The C layer performs almost no validation of its own: it relies on StringValuePtr/NUM2INT conversions to raise TypeError, on Data_Get_Struct without a class check, and on Ruby callers to have vetted names, filenames and SQL. Notable structural facts: the struct is wrapped with a NULL mark function so callables and self references stored only in C (function/aggregate user_data) are not GC-marked through the wrapper; callbacks invoke arbitrary Ruby (and can raise/longjmp) from inside SQLite's C stack; Database#close does not finalize outstanding statements while deallocate does; and sqlite3_open_v2 is hardcoded to READWRITE|CREATE so any filename argument may create files.

ext/sqlite3/database.c:485 - assumes the authorizer's return value is meaningful: anything that is not Fixnum/true/false silently becomes SQLITE_IGNORE at database.c:489, and a raise from the callback is assumed safe to propagate through SQLite's prepare frame
ext/sqlite3/database.c:289 - assumes engine-supplied argc is small and non-negative and that sizeof(VALUE *) is an adequate element size for a VALUE array

ext/sqlite3/database.c:41 - Data_Get_Struct(self, sqlite3Ruby, ctx): Ruby object identity to raw struct pointer; the trust that this VALUE wraps a sqlite3Ruby is established here and reused unchecked by statement.c:36
ext/sqlite3/database.c:68 - process to filesystem/OS: caller strings become an open/create on a path plus VFS selection, crossing from in-process data into persistent state outside the process
ext/sqlite3/database.c:142 - SQLite engine to Ruby (trace): engine-rendered SQL crosses into a host callback as a Ruby String

ext/sqlite3/database.c:237 - SQLite value domain to Ruby object domain in sqlite3val2rb: attacker-influenced column/expression data, including data read from an untrusted database file, becomes Ruby Integer/Float/String, establishing length and type trust for everything downstream
ext/sqlite3/database.c:260 - Ruby to SQLite value domain in set_sqlite3_func_result: arbitrary Ruby return values become SQL results consumed by the query engine

ext/sqlite3/database.c:288 - opaque C pointer to Ruby VALUE via sqlite3_user_data (also database.c:347 and :359): SQLite is trusted to hand back exactly the registered pointer, and that pointer is trusted to still be a valid callable

ext/sqlite3/database.c:468 - engine to Ruby to engine across a security decision: rb_sqlite3_auth converts C strings to Ruby at database.c:478-481 and converts Ruby back into an authorization verdict at database.c:485-489, the highest-consequence boundary because the Ruby side governs SQLite's access control

ext/sqlite3/database.c:541 - database file contents to Ruby runtime state: the PRAGMA encoding row from a possibly untrusted database file selects the Encoding stored in @encoding, which then influences string handling at statement.c:46-49, :119 and :203
ext/sqlite3/database.c:9 - Ruby GC to C resource ownership: deallocate runs during garbage collection and performs SQLite teardown plus xfree, crossing from managed to unmanaged lifetime

ext/sqlite3/exception.c:93 - C error state to Ruby exception: rb_sqlite3_raise, invoked via the CHECK macro at ext/sqlite3/exception.h:4, turns sqlite3_errmsg text into a Ruby exception message (correctly using a "%s" format string), and every CHECK site in database.c (:80, :107, :218, :332, :392, :512, :535) is a non-local-exit point

ext/sqlite3/database.h - read in full (15 lines); defines struct _sqlite3Ruby { sqlite3 *db; } at database.h:6-8, the layout statement.c:36 reinterprets without a type check

ext/sqlite3/sqlite3_ruby.h - read in full; UTF8_P (sqlite3_ruby.h:9) and UTF16_LE_P (:10) are defined only under HAVE_RUBY_ENCODING_H (:6), so the encoding branches at database.c:53 and :63 vanish entirely on builds without it

ext/sqlite3/exception.h - defines the CHECK macro at exception.h:4 used at database.c:80, 107, 218, 332, 392, 512 and 535; it embeds its own semicolon and expands to a call that may raise, so control flow at every use site depends on it

ext/sqlite3/exception.c - read in full; maps SQLite status codes to SQLite3::* classes via rb_path2class and raises at exception.c:93, with SQLITE_OK returning early at exception.c:8 and unknown codes falling through to rb_eRuntimeError

ext/sqlite3/statement.c - the only other consumer of the connection handle; read statement.c:31-69 closely (Data_Get_Struct on the db at :36, closed check at :39, sqlite3_prepare_v2 at :53, @connection retained at :63) plus the implicit calls back into Database#encoding at :46, :119 and :203

lib/sqlite3/database.rb - the Ruby facade deciding what reaches this C code: create_function at database.rb:258-265, create_aggregate/create_aggregate_handler at :303-339 and :387-405 feeding define_function/define_aggregator, authorizer at :73-75, busy_timeout alias at :233, Database.quote defined at :45 but never used, and transaction interpolating mode at :424

lib/sqlite3/pragmas.rb - background for the SQL that reaches this handle: unparameterized PRAGMA construction at pragmas.rb:14, 40, 51-52, 59, 72, 78, 85 and 220, reachable with caller-supplied identifiers via table_info/index_list/index_info/foreign_key_list
output.threat_model.notes: Scope observed: read-only inspection of ext/sqlite3/database.c and ext/sqlite3/database.h plus the files they interact with (sqlite3_ruby.h, exception.c/h, statement.c, lib/sqlite3/database.rb, lib/sqlite3/pragmas.rb, lib/sqlite3/resultset.rb, lib/sqlite3/translator.rb). Nothing was built, executed, installed, fetched, or modified. Confirmed there is no shell, network, or Marshal surface anywhere in lib/ or ext/: the component's untrusted input is exclusively host-application arguments and data returned by the SQLite engine. Per stage instructions no vulnerabilities are asserted; the densest areas for follow-up exploit testing are GC-marking of callback VALUEs (NULL mark at database.c:27 versus user_data at :326 and :384), the sqlite3_trace-versus-sqlite3_busy_handler registration at database.c:215, blob/text length handling at database.c:247-250, and the close/finalize asymmetry at database.c:107.

output.threat_model.summary: SQLite3::Statement is implemented entirely in C (ext/sqlite3/statement.c) and reopened in Ruby (lib/sqlite3/statement.rb). Every Ruby-visible method is an entry point reachable directly by application code: Statement.new receives raw SQL text, bind_param receives arbitrary key/value pairs, and column_name/column_decltype/database_name receive caller-controlled integer indices that are passed to the SQLite C API with no range validation in this file. The struct wrapped by Data_Wrap_Struct holds a raw sqlite3_stmt* with no GC mark function and no back-reference keeping the owning Database alive at the C level, so statement lifetime versus database lifetime is a central modeling concern. Callers in lib/ (Database#execute, #execute_batch, Pragmas#table_info) reach this component with SQL assembled by string interpolation, and Statement#each/ResultSet#next feed decltype strings from the database into the Translator dispatch table.

output.threat_model.summary: SQLite3::Database is the Ruby-side facade over the C extension: it accepts a database file path plus option hash, builds SQL strings (directly and via the Pragmas module), prepares them through the native sqlite3_prepare_v2 wrapper, binds caller-supplied values, registers Ruby callables as SQLite scalar/aggregate functions, tracers, busy handlers and authorizers, and translates result values back into Ruby objects. Trust here is caller-defined: every SQL-text argument (execute, execute_batch, query, prepare, transaction mode, and every pragma name/table/parms argument) is interpolated or passed verbatim, while only positional/named bind variables are parameterized. The second major flow is inbound: bytes stored in the database file and column declared types flow into Translator blocks (Time.parse/Date.parse/DateTime.parse), into pragma default-value unquoting, and into result-hash construction, so a hostile or corrupted database file is untrusted input to Ruby code owned by this component. Authorization is opt-in and delegated to a Ruby callback whose return value is coerced in C, where unexpected values silently become SQLITE_IGNORE.

It handles no request, file, or network input directly; its security relevance is structural. lib/sqlite3.rb:1 performs a LOAD_PATH-relative require of the native extension, so process-level $LOAD_PATH/RUBYLIB configuration decides which shared object is dlopened and initialised with full privilege. errors.rb defines the classes that ext/sqlite3/exception.c resolves via rb_path2class and raises with sqlite3_errmsg(db) as the message, so attacker-influenced text from database content, schema, or SQL is carried into Ruby exception objects and typically onward into logs; the class-level @code is set only on the base class (lib/sqlite3/errors.rb:5), so every subclass reports 0 and callers branching on #code get no discrimination. constants.rb duplicates SQLITE_* values as plain integers with no compile-time linkage to sqlite3.h, and TextRep values flow untouched through Database#create_function/#create_aggregate into sqlite3_create_function, while ColumnType values dispatch decoding of untrusted file contents in value.rb. version.rb hardcodes 1.2.5 in MAJOR/MINOR/TINY while VERSION says 1.2.6, so version-gated compatibility or vulnerability checks in dependents can read inconsistent values, none of which reflect the linked libsqlite3 version.
entryPoints: lib/sqlite3.rb:1 — require 'sqlite3/sqlite3_native' resolves through the ambient $LOAD_PATH (RUBYLIB, -I flags, gem activation), so process configuration rather than an absolute path selects the native object loaded into the interpreter.

lib/sqlite3.rb:2 — require 'sqlite3/database' pulls in the whole public API surface (execute, open, create_function, pragmas, translator); every untrusted input the gem processes reaches the process through the object graph rooted here.
lib/sqlite3/errors.rb:1 — require 'sqlite3/constants' couples the exception hierarchy to the hand-maintained constant table that the C extension also depends on being present and consistent.

ext/sqlite3/exception.c:93 — outside the component's paths but the sole producer of its exception objects: rb_raise(klass, "%s", sqlite3_errmsg(db)) injects a C string derived from database file content, malformed schema, or failing SQL into instances of the classes defined in lib/sqlite3/errors.rb.
lib/sqlite3/pragmas.rb:100 — raise Exception, row[0] uses a value read out of the database (integrity_check result) verbatim as the message of a SQLite3::Exception defined by this component.
sinks: lib/sqlite3.rb:1 — dynamic native-code load; require of a compiled extension is effectively a dlopen sink whose Init_sqlite3_native (ext/sqlite3/sqlite3.c:11) executes with full process privilege.

lib/sqlite3/errors.rb:4 — SQLite3::Exception < ::StandardError is the terminal carrier for unsanitised, untruncated sqlite3_errmsg strings that consumers render into logs, error pages, and trackers (control characters, attacker-chosen identifiers included).

lib/sqlite3/errors.rb:8 — self.code reads a class-level @code assigned only at errors.rb:5; Ruby does not inherit class-level instance variables, so every subclass yields 0 and dependent switch/case error handling collapses to one branch.

lib/sqlite3/constants.rb:3 — TextRep integers are consumed by lib/sqlite3/database.rb:258 and lib/sqlite3/database.rb:304 and forwarded as the eTextRep argument of sqlite3_create_function with no range or validity check on either side.

lib/sqlite3/constants.rb:11 — ColumnType integers are compared against native column types in lib/sqlite3/value.rb:47-51 to pick a conversion path; these are legacy mixed-numbering values, and drift from the linked library causes silent type mis-dispatch on data read from an untrusted database file.

lib/sqlite3/constants.rb:19 — the ErrorCode table hardcodes primary result codes only, omitting extended and post-3.x codes, so callers classifying native statuses with it can misclassify unknown values.

lib/sqlite3/version.rb:10 — STRING derives from MAJOR/MINOR/TINY/BUILD (1.2.5) while lib/sqlite3/version.rb:13 defines VERSION as 1.2.6; both feed packaging and dependent feature/security gating decisions and disagree.
assumptions: lib/sqlite3.rb:1 — assumes $LOAD_PATH has already been constrained to trustworthy directories by RubyGems or the deployer; nothing verifies the loaded object's path or provenance.
lib/sqlite3.rb:2 — assumes the native extension is fully initialised before database.rb reopens SQLite3::Database and SQLite3::Statement; require order is the only enforcement.

lib/sqlite3/errors.rb:4 — assumes exception messages are safe to surface, i.e. that sanitisation of database-derived text happens in the application, though SQLite error strings routinely echo SQL fragments and stored identifier names.
lib/sqlite3/errors.rb:5 — assumes @code is meaningful for the whole hierarchy, an invariant the comments at errors.rb:7 and errors.rb:12 promise but the code never establishes for subclasses.

lib/sqlite3/errors.rb:18 — assumes this exact set of class names in the SQLite3 namespace matches every rb_path2class string at ext/sqlite3/exception.c:12-88; a rename turns an error path into a NameError.

lib/sqlite3/constants.rb:1 — assumes the hand-maintained integer tables stay numerically identical to the sqlite3.h of whatever libsqlite3 ext/sqlite3/extconf.rb links against, with no runtime assertion anywhere.
lib/sqlite3/constants.rb:19 — assumes native statuses are always primary codes in 0..23/100..101; ext/sqlite3/exception.c:89 shows unmapped statuses degrade to a bare RuntimeError.

lib/sqlite3/version.rb:5 — assumes external release tooling keeps the two version representations in sync; the '#:beta-tag:' marker at lib/sqlite3/version.rb:11 shows the file is rewritten out-of-band, so in-repo values are not authoritative.
trustBoundaries: lib/sqlite3.rb:1 — trusted interpreter <- filesystem/$LOAD_PATH-resolved shared object; crossing this boundary executes native initialisation code at full privilege and is the highest-consequence boundary touching the component.

ext/sqlite3/exception.c:93 — libsqlite3 error strings derived from untrusted database files and SQL cross into Ruby objects of classes defined in lib/sqlite3/errors.rb, then into application logging, gaining trust purely by being wrapped in a library exception type.
lib/sqlite3/pragmas.rb:100 — row data read from a possibly user-supplied or corrupted database file crosses into a SQLite3::Exception message consumed as library-authored diagnostic text.

lib/sqlite3/constants.rb:3 — Ruby-side integers leave the managed world and become raw C arguments to sqlite3_create_function via lib/sqlite3/database.rb:258 and lib/sqlite3/database.rb:304, unvalidated on both sides.

lib/sqlite3/constants.rb:11 — native column-type integers describing untrusted file contents cross into the Ruby dispatch table at lib/sqlite3/value.rb:47-51, letting untrusted metadata select which decoding path runs.
lib/sqlite3/version.rb:13 — unverified in-repo literals are accepted downstream as authoritative gem identity for compatibility and vulnerability gating.

lib/sqlite3/constants.rb:1 — 49 lines, read in full; the only in-repo copy of SQLite's enums, to be compared line-by-line against the linked sqlite3.h and against consumers in value.rb and database.rb.
lib/sqlite3.rb:1 — 3 lines, read in full; establishes the native-extension load and the load order on which the gem's entire attack surface hangs.
lib/sqlite3/version.rb:1 — 16 lines, read in full; two disagreeing version representations plus the ':beta-tag:' release-tooling marker.

ext/sqlite3/exception.c:1 — outside the declared paths but must be read in full with errors.rb: sole producer of the component's exceptions, hardcodes the class-name strings, embeds sqlite3_errmsg output at line 93, and degrades unmapped statuses at line 89.
lib/sqlite3/value.rb:40 — primary consumer of Constants::ColumnType; shows how untrusted column-type integers select a conversion path and what happens when no case matches.
lib/sqlite3/database.rb:250 — consumer of Constants::TextRep in create_function (line 258) and create_aggregate (line 304); traces the component's constants across the Ruby-to-C boundary.

output.threat_model.summary: Build/install tooling for the sqlite3-ruby C extension: a small mkmf extconf, two rake task files (native compile via rake-compiler, and a vendoring task that downloads the SQLite amalgamation/DLL over plaintext HTTP and unzips it), and a vendored copy of Minero Aoki's setup.rb 3.3.0 installer. All of it runs at build/install time on the machine of whoever unpacks the gem or checks out the tree, frequently under make or sudo. Untrusted inputs are the developer/CI environment (ENV, ARGV), files inside the source tree that are eval'd or shell-interpolated (metaconfig, pre-/post-task hook scripts, .config, extension directory and file names), network-fetched archives (sqlite.org zips over http, then unzip into the tree), and host toolchain path lookups (wget/curl/unzip/swig/dlltool/make resolved via PATH). Trust boundaries are crossed when zip contents, config-file text, or tree-resident scripts become Ruby code or shell command strings.

setup.rb:698 - `parsearg_global` consumes ARGV to select the task name later dispatched via `__send__ "parsearg_#{task}"` / `__send__ "exec_#{task}"` (setup.rb:648-650).

setup.rb:741 - `parsearg_config` reads ARGV config options; a bare `-`/`--` copies the rest of ARGV verbatim into `@options['config-opt']`, later joined into a shell command line (setup.rb:1072-1074).
setup.rb:767 - `parsearg_install` reads `--prefix=` from ARGV into `@options['install-prefix']`, used as a filesystem path prefix for mkdir/install/chmod.

setup.rb:279 - `ConfigTable#initialize_from_file` parses the on-disk `.config` file (SAVE_FILE at setup.rb:293) with `line.split(/=/,2)`; values flow into `ruby-prog`, `make-prog`, `ruby-path` and all install directories with no key whitelist or validation.
setup.rb:305 - `ConfigTable#[]` recursively expands `$name` references out of the same untrusted table.
setup.rb:654 - `run_metaconfigs` reads `#{@ardir}/metaconfig` from the source tree; per-package variants at setup.rb:881-884.
setup.rb:608 - `run_hook` picks up `pre-/post-<task>` and `.rb` hook scripts from the directory currently being traversed (callers at setup.rb:1281,1287,1293 and 938-967).
setup.rb:1287 - `traverse` walks every subdirectory of bin/lib/ext/data; tree-supplied directory and file names become path components and command arguments.
setup.rb:1197 - `existfiles` collects names from both srcdir and objdir; those names reach `install`, `adjust_shebang` and `chmod` (setup.rb:1150-1165).
ext/sqlite3/extconf.rb:1 - `ENV['RC_ARCHS']` read/overwritten on darwin at extension-configure time.
ext/sqlite3/extconf.rb:7 - `ENV['CC']` copied into `RbConfig::MAKEFILE_CONFIG['CC']`; environment chooses the compiler written into the generated Makefile.
ext/sqlite3/extconf.rb:12 - `dir_config 'sqlite3', ...` accepts `--with-sqlite3-dir/-include/-lib` from the gem-install/extconf command line as include and library search paths.
Rakefile:26 - `ENV['FAT_DIR']` joined into the extension's `lib_dir` output path with no validation.

tasks/vendor_sqlite3.rake:46 - remote input: `http://www.sqlite.org/sqlitedll-<version>.zip` fetched over cleartext HTTP; contents become the DLL shipped in cross-built Windows gems.
tasks/vendor_sqlite3.rake:9 - `Rake::ExtensionCompiler.mingw_gcc_executable` / `mingw_host`: externally configured toolchain locations interpolated into a shell command string.
sinks: setup.rb:470 - `command(str)` executes `system str` as a single string, i.e. full shell interpretation; every build step funnels through here (setup.rb:472).
setup.rb:475 - `ruby(str)` = `command config('ruby-prog') + ' ' + str`; interpreter path comes from `.config` or CLI.
setup.rb:479 - `make(task)` = `command config('make-prog') + ' ' + task`; `make-prog` derived from `configure_args` (setup.rb:141-145) or `.config`.
setup.rb:1072 - `extconf` builds `"#{config('ruby-prog')} #{curr_srcdir()}/extconf.rb #{opt}"` and shells out; interpreter and `config-opt` are unquoted and caller-controlled.

setup.rb:617 - `try_run_hook` runs `instance_eval File.read(fname)`: arbitrary Ruby execution from per-directory hook scripts found during traversal.

setup.rb:439 - `install` writes content to `prefix + dest`, chmods it to the caller's mode (setup.rb:453), and appends the path to `InstalledFiles` (setup.rb:455).
setup.rb:1094 - `adjust_shebang` rewrites executables in place via a predictable temp file `File.basename(path) + '.tmp'` in the CWD (setup.rb:1096).
setup.rb:290 - `ConfigTable#save` writes the `.config` file that a later run re-reads and converts into command strings.
setup.rb:1225 - `_ruby_extentions` selects `.#{Config::CONFIG['DLEXT']}` files from the object dir for installation with mode 0555 (setup.rb:1148-1152).

tasks/vendor_sqlite3.rake:49 - second `system "wget ... || curl ..."` for the DLL archive; same unchecked shell download.
tasks/vendor_sqlite3.rake:59 - `sh "unzip #{full_file}"`: extraction of a network-downloaded zip into `vendor/sqlite3/include` with no entry-path validation or integrity check.
tasks/vendor_sqlite3.rake:75 - `sh "unzip #{full_file}"`: same for the DLL archive into `vendor/sqlite3/lib`.
tasks/vendor_sqlite3.rake:17 - `"#{tool} --dllname #{dllname} --def #{deffile} --output-lib #{libfile}"` returned into `sh` at tasks/vendor_sqlite3.rake:85.
tasks/vendor_sqlite3.rake:24 - MSVC branch `"lib.exe /DEF:#{deffile} /OUT:#{libfile}"`, binary resolved via PATH, executed through `sh`.
tasks/native.rake:28 - `sh "swig -ruby -o #{t.name} #{t.prerequisites.first}"`: code generation by an external PATH-resolved binary; the surrounding `rescue` swallows the real error.
tasks/native.rake:17 - `ext.config_options << "--with-sqlite3-dir=#{sqlite3_lib}"` (cross variant at tasks/native.rake:21): build-time library search path injected into the extconf invocation.
ext/sqlite3/extconf.rb:7 - compiler name from the environment is written into the generated Makefile (`create_makefile` at ext/sqlite3/extconf.rb:26), an execution sink for whoever later runs `make`.
ext/sqlite3/extconf.rb:19 - `find_header`/`find_library` (ext/sqlite3/extconf.rb:19-20) compile and link probe programs, executing the toolchain with caller-supplied paths.
Rakefile:18 - `spec_extras[:extensions] = ["ext/sqlite3/extconf.rb"]` declares the script RubyGems executes on every install of the packaged gem.
